name: Combined Immunodeficiency with Normal B Cells and Normal Immunoglobulins
aliases: Combined Immunodeficiency with Preserved Humoral Immunity

criteria.description: Demonstration of impaired T-cell function by lymphocyte proliferation assays
Normal peripheral B-cell counts by flow cytometry
Normal serum immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, IgM)
History of recurrent or severe infections including opportunistic pathogens
Exclusion of other known immunodeficiencies such as SCID or CVID

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of impaired T-cell function with normal B-cell counts and normal immunoglobulin levels, plus clinical evidence of immunodeficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires comprehensive immunological workup including functional assays and exclusion of other combined immunodeficiencies.

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of T-cell dysfunction despite normal B-cell immunity
Commonly seen in combined immunodeficiencies affecting cellular immunity
searchTerms: fungal infections in weakened immune state
chronic yeast infections on skin and mucous

common.notes: Despite normal immunoglobulins, cellular immunity defects predispose to infections

searchTerms: failure to gain weight as baby
persistent loose stools due to germs

occasional.notes: Immune dysregulation can lead to autoimmune manifestations
May be secondary to chronic infection or immune activation

rare.notes: Rare but severe CNS infections can occur

laboratory: Normal peripheral B-cell counts by flow cytometry
Normal serum immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, IgM)
Impaired T-cell proliferation response to mitogens and antigens
imaging: Chest radiographs showing recurrent pneumonia or bronchiectasis
CT scans may reveal lymphadenopathy or organomegaly
genetic: Mutations in genes affecting T-cell development or function (varies by patient)
No known mutations affecting B-cell development
other: Exclusion of other immunodeficiencies by comprehensive immunophenotyping
Clinical history of recurrent severe infections despite normal humoral immunity

distinguishingFeatures: Severe lymphopenia affecting both B and T cells
Later onset and variable clinical presentation

redFlags: Severe or opportunistic infections despite normal immunoglobulin levels
Failure to thrive in infancy with recurrent infections
Impaired T-cell function demonstrated by laboratory testing
references: Orange JS, et al. Use and interpretation of diagnostic vaccination in primary immunodeficiency: a working group report of the Basic and Clinical Immunology Interest Section of the American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2012.
Picard C, et al. Primary Immunodeficiencies Associated with Severe Defects of the T Cell Compartment: A Review. Front Immunol. 2018.
Orphanet: Combined immunodeficiency with normal B cells and normal immunoglobulins. ORPHA:718079.
